title: Accounts
description: Real bank-account balances, read off the bank at the end of a month — by hand, or through the agent API's record_account_balance, which appends to this same file. Not bookkeeping: there are no transactions here, just "this is what was actually in the account when the month closed". Each account keeps a series of those readings rather than a single one, because the figure carried forward from the last read drifts from the real account and the only cure is to go and look again. A new read is APPENDED, never written over the old one: the history is what lets a past month keep the figure that was true then instead of being re-explained by a number from a year later. The reading in force for a month is the newest one dated before it; months before the earliest reading ignore the account entirely, because a balance nobody has read yet isn't known and isn't guessed. From its anchor the balance is carried forward month by month, so it genuinely depletes. Both pots are modelled and each rolls by its own arithmetic: a private balance by opening + net income - expenses, a company balance by opening + company income - company expenses - employer social - gross salary. In both, "expenses" means the imported statement when actuals cover the whole month, and the budget when they don't — a closed month spends what the bank says it spent, and only a month nobody has imported yet spends what was planned. Every change to this file, hand-edited or written by the agent API, is a git commit.

name.description: What the account is called, shown beside its figure. Must be unique across the file: an account owns a history now, so the same name twice is two histories for one account with no rule for merging them, and it is refused rather than silently summed.

kind.description: Which pot the money is in, spelled the same way budget.json's groups spell it. company: the money the company holds. It enters the ledger straight after Company income and before the employer-social/gross-salary/employee-social/income-tax cascade, so it raises what a full salary can afford — and a negative one lowers it. What the cascade leaves behind is the next month's opening. private: money already drawn. It opens the rolling budget under Net income, as it always has, and is spent down by private expenses. Every account must declare one explicitly; there is no default, because guessing wrong moves real money from one side of the payroll cascade to the other.

balances.description: Every balance ever read off this account, newest or oldest first as you like — the order in the file carries no meaning and they are sorted on read. Two readings in the same month are refused: they would be two candidate openings for one month with nothing to choose between them. Keeping the old entries costs nothing and is the point of the list, so append rather than replace.

as_of.description: The month-end date this balance was read, e.g. "2026-07-31": the LAST day of the month, always. It is the CLOSING balance of that month, read at the end of that day, so it becomes the OPENING balance of the next one — a balance dated 2026-07-31 is August's starting figure, usable in August immediately, and has no effect on July. There is no such thing as a mid-month balance here: half a month is not a closing figure, because the rest of that month's spending has not happened yet, and only the month is read anyway. The write API refuses any other day outright; a file with one is read as the month's figure regardless, which is exactly the misreading the rule exists to prevent.

balance.description: Euros, decimals allowed (e.g. 1427.42). May be negative for an overdrawn account.

note.description: Free-text context for this one reading, shown next to the account name in the month it anchors. Not used in any computation.
